newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh refugees to leave India from late March.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh refugees to leave India from late March.

text.p: Bangladesh tribespeople who have fled into India to escape a long-running insurgency will start returning home on March 28, officials said on Monday.

They said the date was agreed on at talks between refugee leader Upendralal Chakma and a Bangladesh parliamentary delegation led by Abul Hasanat Abdullah held in northeast India's Tripura state over the past few days.
An estimated 50,000 tribal refugees from Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts region have lived for years in Tripura, also the headquarters of tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas.
Some 5,000 refugees are expected to return on March 28, one official, who declined to be identified, said. He could not give a date for the return of the next group.
"It may take some days because the refugee leaders and the Shanti Bahini would like to see how the rehabilitation of the returnees is going on," said the official.

The Shanti Bahini has been fighting government forces in the Hill Tracts region, which borders India and Burma, since 1973. They demand political autonomy and the expulsion of some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers who have moved into their traditional homeland from other parts of Bangladesh.

Officials said the government had pledged to help the refugees resettle in the Hill Tracts by giving them cash and food rations for nine months. They will also regain their land and previous jobs under the repatriation deal.
About 6,000 refugees returned under a similar deal in February 1994 but the process was abruptly halted in what the government said was a unilateral decision by the Shanti Bahini.
The new deal comes one-and-a-half months after Bangladesh held peace talks in Dhaka with the rebel group's political wing. The talks are due to resume on Wednesday.
Several tribal groups staged a rally in Dhaka on Monday to reiterate their demand for "full autonomy" of the Hill Tracts and the "rehabilitation of Bengalis elsewhere".

"These people (Bengalis) did not come to the Hill Tracts on their own. They were pushed here by successive governments on false promises...," said a joint statement by the Hill People's Council, the Hill Students' Council and Hill Women's Federation.
They also demanded the armed forces be gradually withdrawn from the Hill Tracts, a bone of contention in the peace drive.
Government officials said Bengali settlers had called for a general strike on Wednesday in three Hill Tracts districts to pressure authorities not to force them out of the area.
Bangladesh has thus far refused rebel demands to expel the settlers, fearing a violent backlash.
